required_starting_state.description: Displayed identities for one recognizable seeded Component of every supported kind.
The unique disposable Component name used by the scenario.
The exact light/dark 1280/768/390, keyboard, 200% zoom, no-JavaScript, hydration, and console matrix.

steps.action: Open Components from navigation and open every supported seeded kind.
steps.expected_result: Each list/detail/view route loads with canonical Components wording and recognizable output.

steps.action: Create the disposable Component, edit it, publish a new version, and open its view.
steps.expected_result: Each action succeeds and the published view reflects the saved change.

steps.action: Exercise the allowed lifecycle actions, then remove the disposable record.
steps.expected_result: State changes are clear and cleanup succeeds.

steps.action: At 1280, 768, and 390 CSS pixels, inspect the directory, editor, detail, and viewer in both light and dark themes; capture the named evidence.
steps.expected_result: Layout, structured controls, table/visual output, focus, contrast, and vocabulary match the accepted baseline with no horizontal overflow or hidden required action.

steps.action: Use keyboard-only navigation through filters, editor controls, preview, lifecycle confirmation, and back/forward; repeat a representative directory/editor/view flow at 200% browser zoom.
steps.expected_result: Focus order and restoration are visible, dialogs are operable, and zoom does not hide content or require two-dimensional scrolling.

steps.action: Disable JavaScript and directly load manager and reader Component URLs, then re-enable JavaScript and repeat direct load/back/forward while recording the console.
steps.expected_result: SSR is useful and role-correct without JavaScript; hydration/navigation preserve content with no hydration or browser-console errors.

required_starting_state.description: Authorization for the exact tessara-sprint-8a disposable project.
Resolved project, database, volume, network, and service identities.
The frozen candidate source identity.

steps.action: Run the approved from-empty materialization.
steps.expected_result: Owners initialize and seed in declared order; the topology becomes healthy.

steps.action: Inspect owner read-back and open Components plus the seeded Dashboard.
steps.expected_result: Exactly seven Component shells and eight versions exist: the Stat Card `1.0.0` predecessor is superseded/inactive and names the published/active `2.0.0` successor; the other six versions are published/active.

steps.action: Inspect the seeded Dashboard placements and their resolved references.
steps.expected_result: Exactly seven placements exist: four normal/blocked-scope fixtures plus independent `lifecycle-upgrade`, `lifecycle-replace`, and `lifecycle-remove` placements bound to the inactive predecessor; every reference is selected-instance Components v3.

steps.action: Inspect module inventory and navigation.
steps.expected_result: Dashboard appears once through its real Release/Instance; Core has exactly Forms, Workflows, Responses, Datasets, and Migration transitions.

steps.action: Repeat bootstrap unchanged.
steps.expected_result: The receipt reports an exact semantic no-op with no duplicate rows, revisions, references, roles, or configuration.

required_starting_state.description: The original Components display label.
The original Dataset timeout.
The exact temporary label Visual Parts and timeout 6.

steps.action: Confirm the initial Manifest-driven values, then save `Visual Parts` and timeout `6`.
steps.expected_result: Defaults are `Components` and `5`; navigation/admin show the temporary label; product headings remain Components; diagnostics show redacted effective values.

steps.action: Try blank/81-character labels, timeouts 0/31, an unknown field, and unsupported schema version.
steps.expected_result: Every invalid value is rejected without clamping or partial save.

steps.action: Repeat as a reader and as a Components manager without global configuration authority.
steps.expected_result: Read access follows role; unauthorized writes are denied.

steps.action: Inspect diagnostics after a compatibility-dependent Component operation.
steps.expected_result: The selected `tessara.components.dataset-major-line` binding, Core-installation provider, contract ID/version, compatibility, health, observation time, and stable result/failure code appear; raw Dataset references, rows, counts, credentials, and secrets do not.

steps.action: Restore the recorded settings.
steps.expected_result: Original configuration and navigation are restored.

required_starting_state.description: The displayed identity of the allowed Dataset.
The displayed identity of the out-of-scope Dataset.
The prepared mixed Dashboard and exact shared/disjoint placements.
The disposable draft with an unsaved visible change.

steps.action: Preview, save, publish, and execute using the allowed Dataset.
steps.expected_result: Operations succeed through the canonical typed reference.

steps.action: As an administrator or another actor authorized on both scopes, open the mixed Dashboard. Render the shared scope-A placement, inspect the disjoint scope-B tile, and try its render action.
steps.expected_result: The shared placement discloses its exact Component identity and renders normally. The disjoint placement is generic and unavailable, discloses no Component/Dataset identity, scope, title, or data, and its render is denied.

steps.action: Try the out-of-scope record and wrong-role account, then compare a known blocked direct identity with a generated random identity.
steps.expected_result: Access is denied without revealing whether a restricted resource exists; the known and random public outcomes are equivalent.

steps.action: Stop or timeout the Dataset provider, then retry preview/save.
steps.expected_result: Existing metadata remains readable; dependent mutations do not persist; unsaved input remains.

steps.action: Restore the provider and retry.
steps.expected_result: Readiness returns and the valid operation succeeds once.

scenarios.role: Operator, Component manager, Dashboard manager, and reader

actor_bindings.role: Operator authorized to stop and restore the disposable Component provider

required_starting_state.description: The exact Reference Operations Dashboard identity.
The upgrade, replace, remove, and blocked-scope placement IDs.
The superseded predecessor and its declared published successor.
The unrelated route used to prove outage containment.

steps.action: Refresh dependency health before any action.
steps.expected_result: Exactly three `lifecycle_unrenderable` findings appear for the three action placements. The blocked-scope placement is absent, while the authorized upgrade finding discloses the declared successor.

steps.action: Defer the upgrade fixture, refresh it at the returned finding revision, then choose Upgrade.
steps.expected_result: Defer advances the finding revision and remains actionable; Upgrade resolves it by using the declared successor.

steps.action: On the independent fixtures, Replace with the authorized current Table reference and Remove the remove placement.
steps.expected_result: Replace and Remove each resolve only its selected placement; the three action paths do not consume one another's fixture.

steps.action: Stop only the Sprint 8A Component provider, refresh the Dashboard, and open the unrelated route.
steps.expected_result: Exactly five remaining authorized placements report `provider_unavailable`; the blocked placement remains absent and the unrelated route stays healthy.

steps.action: Restore Components, wait for readiness, and refresh.
steps.expected_result: Dashboard health is `healthy`, open/deferred counts are zero, and no visible finding remains.

steps.action: Record the structured dependency-semantic receipt and restore the canonical fresh seed as directed by the coordinator.
steps.expected_result: The authenticated JSON receipt contains every exact check/action identity and requires canonical reset; restoration is recorded without converting this manual scenario into rehearsal evidence.

scenarios.role: Operator plus authorized and restricted users

required_starting_state.description: The retained v1, v2, Core owner/type, retired missing_policy alias, flat Dataset-major fields, and old-payload negative inputs.
The selected Component Release and Instance shown in Module Management.

steps.action: Review inventory, routes, process, database, manifest, and provenance.
steps.expected_result: Components and Dashboard each appear as real deployed modules; Dashboard appears once; Core exposes no Component product owner.

steps.action: Submit each approved old reference/payload, including `missing_policy` and flat Dataset-major fields, as an authorized user.
steps.expected_result: Each is rejected by the exact v3/typed-reference contract; no normalization helper, alias, adapter, ledger, copied-count expectation, or fallback is shown.

steps.action: Repeat known and random restricted inputs as the restricted user.
steps.expected_result: Responses are indistinguishable and disclose no protected identity.

The exact prerequisite expected to fail.

steps.action: Run materialization with the approved fault.
steps.expected_result: The attempt fails at the intended point and retains raw apply response and service logs.

steps.action: Inspect containers, named volumes, and networks after teardown.
steps.expected_result: No resource belonging to `tessara-sprint-8a` remains.

steps.action: Remove the fault and run a complete new materialization.
steps.expected_result: A new empty attempt reaches canonical health; no partial state is reused.

steps.action: Repeat bootstrap unchanged.
steps.expected_result: The successor reports an exact semantic no-op.

steps.action: Apply the `1.0.0` selection and exercise Component plus Dashboard routes.
steps.expected_result: The exact `0.9.0` to `1.0.0` upgrade is health-gated; recorded Component data/configuration and placements remain usable.

steps.action: Compare the pre-transition and post-upgrade snapshots.
steps.expected_result: Core, gateway, Supervisor, Dashboard, Dataset compatibility, and other modules retain image/container/restart, semantic data, navigation, and availability identity.

steps.action: Apply rollback to `0.9.0`, verify health/behavior, then restore intended `1.0.0`.
steps.expected_result: Each plan remains Component-only and health-gated; release read-back matches each stage; final state is healthy intended `1.0.0`; publish the authenticated upgrade/rollback JSON receipt.
